Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

A reviewer claims the following defect in the NEW code. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the actual files. Default to refuted=true when you cannot demonstrate a concrete failure.

TITLE: Eviction can steal the caller's own user pages mid-syscall; the resulting S-mode page fault deadlocks on the non-recursive kernel lock
FILE: Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c
CLAIM: do_exec() (sched.c:185-256) calls enable_sum() at line 189 and keeps user pointers `file_name` and `argv[]` (which point into the *caller's* address space) live across init_page_table() (line 219, ~6 frames), alloc_user_page() for the kernel stack (line 221) and load_elf() (line 244, more frames). Every one of those may run alloc_user_page -> selete_page(), and selete_page (mm.c:104-116) skips only `pin` and `pgtable == NULL` frames — the shell's own stack page holding argv[i] and the argv strings is an ordinary unpinned frame and is a legal victim. init_user_stack() then dereferences it at sched.c:156-158 (`strlen(argv[i])`, `memcpy(..., argv[i], len)`). Because the page is now _PAGE_SOFT, that load traps in S-mode; exception_handler_entry unconditionally executes `call lock_kernel` (arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:199) and lock_kernel is a plain non-recursive spin_lock_acquire (kernel/sched/smp.c:30, kernel/locking/lock.c:9-17) that this hart already holds — both harts wedge forever, with no console output. Nothing pins the caller's argv/file_name pages (or copies them into kernel memory) for the duration of the call, and handle_page_fault has no way to report failure. The same hazard applies to do_process_show/do_show_exec, which write into a user buffer under SUM.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

I have verified the claim against the actual files. Here is what I found.

**The pivotal guard the claim overlooks: `do_exec` refuses to run unless there are ≥16 free frames, and it only ever allocates 7.**

`/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c:253` (before *any* allocation, after the pcb-slot search):

```c
if (free_page_num() < EXEC_MIN_FREE_PAGES) {   /* EXEC_MIN_FREE_PAGES == 16 (line 43) */
    disable_sum(); enable_preempt(); return -2;
}
```

Frame accounting for everything that follows that check:
- `init_page_table()` (`/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c`, `USER_CODE_BEGIN 0xf000` → `USER_CODE_END 0x14000`): 5 code pages + 1 stack page = **6** user frames. Its page-table pages come from the separate `pgdir_page[]` pool (`FREE_PGDIR_ADDR`), not `user_page[]`.
- kernel stack `alloc_user_page(1, NULL)`: **1** frame (pinned).
- `load_elf(..., alloc_page_helper)`: **0 new frames.** I parsed all five images in `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/test/*.elf`: each has exactly one `PT_LOAD`, `vaddr = 0xf000`, largest `memsz = 0x3e98` (test_shell) → end `0x12e98`. `load_elf` steps `p_memsz` by 4096, so it calls the callback for 0xf000/0x10000/0x11000/0x12000 — all already present, and `alloc_page_helper` is a no-op on a present PTE.
- `init_user_stack()`: `alloc_page_helper(USER_STACK_ADDR - PAGE_SIZE, ...)` on the page `init_page_table()` already mapped → **0 new frames**.

Total = **7 frames, with ≥16 guaranteed free**. `alloc_user_page` only calls `selete_page()` on the `i == USER_PAGE_NUM` branch, i.e. when *not a single* frame is free. With ≥9 frames still free when `do_exec` returns, that branch is unreachable from `do_exec`, so no eviction — of the caller's argv page or anything else — can happen between `enable_sum()` and `disable_sum()`.

**No concurrent allocator can shrink the margin either.** The global kernel lock is taken in `arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:199` and released only in `ret_from_exception`; `do_exec` never releases it and never calls `scheduler()`. The only kernel code that runs outside the trap path is `init/main.c`'s idle loop (which calls `free_user_page` only — frees raise `free_page_num()`) and `smp_init`'s `wfi` loop. So `free_page_num()` is conservative here.

**The `do_process_show`/`do_show_exec` extension is also wrong on its own terms.** I read both (`sched.c:487` and `sched.c:644`): they are pure `strcat`/`itoa` into the user buffer and allocate nothing, so there is no allocation for an eviction to hang off — the "same hazard" does not apply.

**Global exhaustion, the precondition for the whole mechanism, is not reachable in this configuration.** `USER_PAGE_NUM = (0x5e000000 - 0x51000000)/4096 = 53248` frames (208 MB). The heaviest test, `test/swap.c`, touches `4096*8` longs = 64 pages; `NUM_MAX_TASK` is 16 and each process costs ~7 frames. Nothing in the tree comes within three orders of magnitude of exhausting `user_page[]`, so `selete_page()` never runs at all — and if it somehow did, the shell's hot stack page carries `_PAGE_ACCESSED` (set by `alloc_page_helper` and by hardware), so the NRU second-chance loop would have to sweep it twice.

I do confirm the *consequence* half of the claim is mechanically accurate — `entry.S:199` calls `lock_kernel` unconditionally and `spin_lock_acquire` (`kernel/locking/lock.c`) is non-recursive, so an S-mode fault while holding the lock would wedge. But that is a property of the given, unmodifiable framework, and the new code contains a guard that makes the claimed trigger unreachable. The only residual path would be a user pointer that was *already* swapped out before syscall entry — a different mechanism from the one claimed, and itself unreachable for the memory-size reason above.
